differences.what: massing: a flat three-bay front of two storeys over a high basement, its south face showing past its south corner
differences.how: T-1872: the 1911 sheet's 10.65 m front at the camera's 11.74 px/m (x 1845-1970 px in both), its heights from the drawing's proportions: the principal floor's string course at y 549 px in the drawing and 551 in the render, the cornice's crown at y 400 and about 404

differences.what: the door in the middle bay, round-headed, at the head of a stoop running straight out to the walk
differences.how: T-1872: was in the south bay, flat-headed; now K07's round-headed entrance under a voussoir ring in the middle bay, its crown at y 503-505 px in both, the stoop straight out from it
T-1872: K11 stoop rails each side of an open stoop (no stone cheeks), as drawn

differences.what: the principal floor's outer bays: a pair of round-headed lights under one arched head
differences.how: T-1872: was one flat-headed sash in a K09 surround; now K06's paired round-headed sash under a voussoir ring, sills y 546 and 545 px, crowns y 507 in both

differences.what: the basement: a pair of round-headed lights under each outer bay
differences.how: T-1872: was one square area light; now a pair of K06 round-headed basement lights, y 562-585 px in the drawing and 562-583 in the render

differences.what: the second storey: three round-arched windows, one a bay, the outer two drawn in toward the middle
differences.how: T-1872: was three flat-headed sash; now K06 single round-headed sash, crowns y 437 and sills y 480 px in both, the outer two set 0.5 m and 0.35 m in, their glass at x 1868-1880 and 1937-1948 px in the render against 1866-1881 and 1935-1950 in the drawing

differences.what: the balcony over the door, its rail under the second storey's middle window
differences.how: T-1872: was missing; now a stone slab on two consoles with an iron guard across the middle bay, its rail y 483-500 px in the render against 482-497 in the drawing

differences.what: the bracketed cornice over a plain frieze, its crown about 2 m over the upstairs windows' crowns
differences.how: T-1872: the K10 bracketed timber cornice, its brackets hanging to y 418 px in the render and 420 in the drawing, once the second storey was raised to the drawing's proportion (the cornice had stood about 1 m low)

differences.what: no dormer on the hip's street slope
differences.how: T-1872: the K05 street dormer is removed; the sheet's half storey is an attic under the hip

differences.what: one tall stack rising behind the front near its north end
differences.how: T-1872: was two stacks in the north wall; the front one is removed, and the rear one draws at x 1925-1937 px against the drawing's 1927-1945

differences.what: the hip's height: the drawing draws the roof's top about 1.8 m over the cornice's crown (y 368 against 400 px), the render about 3.8 m (y 332); the stack's top follows it, about 1.8 m higher than drawn (y 310 against 342 px)
differences.how: T-1872: the hip is at 25 degrees, the K01 contract's lowest for an ordinary roof; the drawing's roof reads as about 20 degrees, which the contract refuses (k01_contract.json roof pitch_deg ranges.ordinary [25, 45]). Closing it needs that range widened for a low Italianate hip, a decision for the component standard

differences.what: the bracketed cornice's projection and the frieze's depth
differences.how: the drawing's crown stands at about the render's (y 400 against 404 px, 0.2 m) and its brackets end where the render's do; their exact profile is K10's

differences.what: the arched heads drawn as dark hood moulds without keystones; the render lays voussoir rings with short keys
differences.how: the rings run round each head where the drawing's hoods do; the keys are 0.2-0.3 m wide, 2-3 px at the drawing's scale

differences.what: the drawing hatches the south part of the upper front
differences.how: a cast shadow or the artist's shading across the lit front, not a recess: the front's face runs straight across it at every storey below

the south face's openings, the frame porch on the south wall, the rear and the rear wing
